title: Fraunces Tavern

nativeAxes.x: west-southwest along Pearl Street toward Broad Street

identityStatus: 54 Pearl Street / 99 Broad Street corner block matched using five-bay red Pearl Street facade and five-bay buff Broad Street facade; 101 Broad and 58 Pearl are distinct neighbors.

properties.scope: Main three-story corner block; exclude the narrow rear/east mapped connector to later museum properties.

geometryLabel: Mapped main corner block, clipped at the rear wall shared with 101 Broad Street; neighboring museum buildings and narrow connector excluded.

orientationControl.basis: Street-facing red and buff brick facades match local photographs, official 1965 designation and 1978 district boundary map.

terrainContact.basis: Pearl Street sidewalk outside the central columned entrance portico.

source: Protomaps/OpenStreetMap footprint and coarse roof height, local Qualla exterior photographs, NYC LPC 1965 designation and 1978 district report/map.
notes: The mapped 14.6 m height is treated as an approximate roof/balustrade control; chimneys rise above it. Three stories and attic, twelve-over-twelve sash, red jack arches, paneled cornice, truncated roof platform and balustrade follow the official description and photographs. The narrow mapped connection continuing south is outside this individual building scope.
limitations: Not a survey. Vertical dimensions, hidden roof surfaces and exact brick/baluster profiles are approximations.
The 2010–2014 local photos represent the restored exterior; no exact reconstruction of the 1783 building is claimed.
Scope cut excludes the narrow rear connector from a larger connected map polygon.
